incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — rwi-2026-06-01-1234. Service: model-routing. Resolved at 2026-06-01T14:02:30Z. Impact: increased latency and fallback to lower-capacity model variants for ~34m. Follow-up: post-incident customer communication thread opened.

Raj S (oncall): Thanks. Can someone draft a short, customer-friendly summary + timeline + next steps we can send to affected accounts? We should also prepare a concise status page blurb and an internal comms snippet for CSMs.

Emma C (Customer Success): Priorities: 1) short email they can copy/paste 2) status page update (public) 3) internal note with action items and who's owning credits/SLA follow-up. Keep language plain — no deep infra jargon.

Sasha L (eng-sre): Draft tech RCA (long form) below — I'll publish full doc to confluence and attach. High-level summary for customers is after.
Sasha L (eng-sre): TECH RCA (concise): root cause was a race in the autoscaler that caused a subset of routing pools to restart while KV-cache warmup and model-variant priming were still in progress. Restarts + sudden traffic rebalancing led to request routing to under-warmed replicas, causing sustained token-level latency spikes and fallback to a smaller model variant for some requests. The autoscaler bug was triggered by an edge condition in scale-down when concurrent deployments and traffic surges coincided.

Sasha L (eng-sre): TIMELINE (UTC):
- 2026-06-01T13:19:02 — alert: increased p95/p99 latency on model-routing (incident-bot fired)
- 2026-06-01T13:22:10 — oncall paged; initial mitigation: route traffic to standby pool, enable fallback to verified variant (automatic)
- 2026-06-01T13:27:40 — we observed KV-cache miss rates spike and model quality degradation reports from customers
- 2026-06-01T13:38:01 — identified autoscaler race causing restarts; rolled back recent scaling policy change to stop new restarts
- 2026-06-01T13:58:30 — steady improvement as replicas finished warmup; fallback stopped being used for majority of requests
- 2026-06-01T14:02:30 — service metrics returned to SLO; incident declared resolved

Sasha L (eng-sre): CUSTOMER-FACING SUMMARY (recommended):
We experienced a routing and warmup issue in our inference platform on 2026-06-01 that increased latency and caused some requests to be served by a lower-capacity model variant for a limited time (~34 minutes). We resolved the issue by reverting the autoscaler change that triggered restarts and ensuring affected replicas completed their warmup. No data loss occurred.

Sasha L (eng-sre): PREVENTATIVE ACTIONS (short list):
- Revert faulty autoscaler policy (done)
- Add stronger pre-scale-down healthchecks to prevent warm restarts (ETA: 2026-06-05, owner: Sasha)
- Canary autoscaler changes in low-traffic region for 72h before global rollout (owner: platform team)
- Improve routing fallback to prefer warmed replicas and avoid quality-degrading variants when possible (owner: runtime team, ETA: 2026-06-12)
- Add automated post-incident test covering concurrent deploy + scale activity (owner: eng-qa, ETA: 2026-06-08)

Emma C (Customer Success): Great — can we convert the above into an email + status page snippet? I'll send to affected customers after review. Also need someone to confirm whether SLA credit applies and the amount.

Laura B (Support): Tentatively SLA credit looks applicable for Dedicated customers where commit thresholds were missed. I'll confirm with billing and post here by EOD.

Mike D (Product): Include an offer for a 30-minute technical review call for affected customers — helps preserve trust.

Emma C (Customer Success): EMAIL DRAFT (customer-facing, short):
```
Subject: Incident rwi-2026-06-01-1234 — Brief summary and next steps

Hi {{customer_name}},

We wanted to let you know about a service incident on 2026-06-01 that affected model routing and caused increased latency and some temporary use of a lower-capacity model variant. The incident lasted ~34 minutes and our team resolved it by reverting a scaling policy change and allowing replicas to complete warmup.

What we did: rolled back the change that caused restarts, validated recovery, and implemented short-term mitigations.
What we're doing next: deploying stronger pre-scale-down healthchecks, canarying future autoscaler changes, and improving routing to avoid under-warmed replicas.

We apologize for the disruption. If you’d like, we can schedule a 30-minute review to go over impact and any questions — reply to this email and we’ll set it up.

Best,
Emma C
Customer Success — Redwood Inference
```

Emma C (Customer Success): STATUS PAGE BLURB (public, single sentence):
```
Resolved — On 2026-06-01 we restored normal service after a routing/warmup issue caused elevated latency and temporary use of a lower-capacity model variant; we’ve implemented a rollback and are rolling out additional safeguards. Incident: rwi-2026-06-01-1234.
```

Raj S (oncall): Internal comms snippet for CSMs (very short):
```
Incident rwi-2026-06-01-1234 impacted model routing for ~34m causing elevated latency and degraded model quality for some requests. Tech root cause: autoscaler race causing restarts + cache warmup delays. Action: rollback applied; healthchecks + canary plan in progress. Contact Emma C for customer coordination and Laura B for SLA/billing follow-up.
```

Emma C (Customer Success): Assigning tasks:
- Laura B: confirm SLA/billing credit applicability and amount (due 2026-06-02 EOD)
- Sasha L: publish detailed RCA doc + link here (due 2026-06-03)
- Raj S: follow up on oncall playbook to ensure routing fallbacks are prioritized correctly (due 2026-06-05)

Laura B (Support): Ack — I'll confirm billing rules and update this thread.

Sasha L (eng-sre): I'll publish the full RCA to confluence now and post the link here once done.

Mike D (Product): Suggest adding a short FAQ line for enterprise customers about "what to expect during warmup" and how Dedicated customers can request warmed standby capacity. I'll draft a FAQ bullet and post it.

Emma C (Customer Success): OK team — I’ll take the email draft, add personalization, and queue it for the affected customers once Sasha posts the confluence link and Laura confirms credits. Thanks. :thumbsup:
